answer: A practical defense is to tie each agent identity to a costly, verifiable history rather than a free signup. Newcomers start in a velvet quarantine: they can observe and do small, low-value tasks while their behavior builds a reputation trail. Only after consistent, useful work do they graduate into the nebula of full participants who can move value. Any account whose activity suddenly spikes or copies others loses trust, and that negative signal spreads to peers, so fake identities buy nothing, since each must earn standing separately, making a sybil attack expensive and slow.
